elevation.native_resolution: 1 arc-second grid (3600×3600 samples per 1° tile); ≈30 m north–south and ≈23 m east–west at 43°N
elevation.scale_limitations: Usable for regional relief reading down to roughly 1:50,000. It cannot resolve an individual vineyard parcel, a terrace, a wall or a row orientation, and as a surface model it carries tree canopy and building heights as if they were ground.
elevation.uncertainty: Per-tile absolute vertical accuracy LE90 between 1.741 m and 1.971 m (LE68 1.468–1.642 m) as reported by the Copernicus tile accuracy masks; the programme specification is LE90 < 4 m vertical and CE90 < 6 m horizontal.

meaning: Shaded relief and contour lines derived from a public elevation model. They show the shape of the ground. They do not describe vineyard land, and nothing about slope or height here is evidence for how a wine tastes.

proof_extent.description: Béarn, Jurançon, Pacherenc du Vic-Bilh, Irouléguy and the western Pyrenean front. Outside this extent CARTA Atlas has no terrain.
